notes: internal/auth/auth.go:57 — MinPasswordLength now counts runes (utf8.RuneCountInString); the 72-byte bcrypt cap is unchanged. auth_test.go additions fail on origin/main ('a four-character passphrase was accepted because it is twelve bytes') and pass on HEAD — verified by swapping the file.

internal/httpapi/admin.go:892-970 — PATCH /api/v1/users/{id} accepts an optional `password`. Guards verified: orgAdmin middleware (session only, api_key refused) unchanged; new RoleAbove(current, caller) check means an organization_admin can no longer set a super_admin's password, demote or disable one (403); self-reset is 400 SELF_PASSWORD; PasswordProblem applied before hashing; hash settled before the UPDATE; user_sessions swept after; audit detail carries only role + password_reset bool, never the password. Unknown id now 404 instead of a silent 200 — small behavior change, tested.

integration_password_reset_test.go runs against a real Postgres (spun up postgres:16-alpine locally; MOMENTO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN set) through the real Handler(): all 6 subtests pass on HEAD, and on origin/main 5 of 6 fail (unknown field `password`, weak passwords replacing the hash, org_admin editing super_admin, 404). Deny paths (weak/too-long, superior account, self, unknown id) all execute real assertions.

Full `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` with DB: all packages ok except internal/service TestMaintenanceFailsARebuildOutOfAttempts, which failed once with a deadlock-victim race and passed 3/3 reruns — pre-existing flake in a package this PR does not touch.

web: npm test 100/100 including the 3 new passwordRule tests; tsc -b and eslint clean on the changed files. Frontend rule (Array.from().length ≥ 12, TextEncoder bytes ≤ 72) matches the server's rune/byte bounds; every server write path (updateMe, createUser, updateUser) uses auth.PasswordProblem.
Default-off in effect: no setting, no migration, no new public route; the field only acts when an administrator explicitly sends a non-empty password. Code-only change, fully revertible.

Observation, not a defect: the server does not refuse a password reset on an OIDC-linked account (UI hides the field; docs say only that the field is not shown). Accounts holding both oidc_subject and password_hash already exist in the model (OIDC login ON CONFLICT(email) keeps the local hash), and the caller must already hold organization_admin, so this does not widen authority beyond what createUser grants. Worth a follow-up if the operator wants SSO-only accounts enforced server-side.

Behavior tightening to be aware of on release: organization_admin can no longer edit any field (display_name, department, active) of a super_admin — 403 ROLE_ABOVE_CALLER. Documented in ADMIN_GUIDE 4.2.
